given: A form control and its visible label are present
when: Navigate to the control with a screen reader and inspect its programmatic label
then: The label is associated with the intended control; group labels are available where applicable

given: Text is shown on each supported component background
when: Measure the rendered text and background colors in the relevant states
then: Ordinary text has at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text has at least 3:1; record applicable criterion exceptions

given: The component contains text and interactive controls
then: The component retains its information and functionality; record criterion exceptions such as captions and images of text

given: The component is in a page with vertically scrolling content
when: Set the layout viewport to 320 CSS pixels wide or equivalent zoom and use all controls
then: Content remains usable without scrolling in two dimensions; document any content that requires a two-dimensional layout

given: A visual cue is needed to identify a control or its state
when: Measure that cue against adjacent colors in each relevant state
then: Required cues have at least 3:1 contrast; document applicable inactive-control or unmodified browser-appearance exceptions

given: The component has an interactive function
when: Use the documented keyboard interactions for that function
then: The function can be completed with a keyboard; record any criterion exception for inherently path-dependent input

given: Keyboard focus is inside the component
when: Use Tab, Shift+Tab, or the documented exit interaction
then: Focus can leave through an available keyboard interaction; any nonstandard exit method is explained to the user

given: The component includes multiple focusable controls
when: Move forward and backward through controls and exercise interactions that move focus
then: The focus sequence preserves meaning and operability; record the expected sequence for the component

given: The component is visible and supports keyboard interaction
when: Move keyboard focus to each interactive element
then: A visible indicator identifies the focused element

given: The component detects an invalid user entry
then: A text message identifies the affected input and describes the error

given: The component is rendered in a known state
when: Navigate to its controls with a screen reader and change their states
then: Each control exposes its intended name and role; applicable values and state changes are available to assistive technology
